9012792: As part of a research study on student use of LLMs in programming assignments, a research team is seeking your permission to use data from assignments submitted as part of this class.
Title of research study: LLM Assignment Use Analysis
Principal Investgator: Cliff Shaffer, shaffer@vt.edu, 540-231-4354.
Key Information: This study will make use of assignments that you submit as a regular part of this class. No additional work is needed on your part to participate in the study. All assignment data will be de-identified prior to beginning any analysis, and the data will not be re-identified at any time. Your decision to participate or not participate will have no bearing on your grade or relationship with Virginia Tech. The research team won’t know who participated until after grades have been turned in.
Detailed Information: The following is more detailed information about this study in addition to the information listed above. The information to be studied include content from your course assignments, including these LLM use surveys and your scores on various assignments. Once the information for an individual has been aggregated, all identifying information is removed prior to analysis of the data. No attempt to later re-identify the data will be made. The only data stored will be the de-identified, aggregated data for the entire class. Federal laws state that you must give permission for researchers to access your school records. By giving consent to participate, you are also providing consent to access the following school records: These LLM survey responses and scores for assignments submitted for this class. If identifiers are removed from your private information, that information could be used for future research studies or distributed to another investigator for future research studies without your additional informed consent. Thisrelease will be kept indefinitely.
Who can I talk to?If you have questions, concerns, or complaints, or think the research has hurt you, talk to the research team by contacting shaffer@vt.edu.This research has been reviewed and approved by the Virginia Tech Institutional Review Board (IRB). You may communicate with them at 540-231-3732 or irb@vt.edu if:●  You have questions about your rights as a research subject●  Your questions, concerns, or complaints are not being answered by the research team●  You cannot reach the research team●  You want to talk to someone besides the research team to provide feedback about this research
How many people will be studied?We plan to include about 800-1000 people in this research study.
What happens if I say yes, I want to be in this research? You do not need to do anything different regardless of whether you agree to allow use of your data or not. All data used comes from assignments that you do as a normal part of the course.
What happens if I say yes, but I change my mind later? You may contact the study team at shaffer@vt.edu later to ask that your data not be used.
Is there any way being in this study could be bad for me? There are no known risks to participating in this study.
What happens to the information collected for the research?We will make every effort to limit the use and disclosure of your personal information only to people who have a need to review this information. We cannot promise complete confidentiality. Organizations that may inspect and copy your information include the IRB, Human Research Protection Program, and other authorized representatives of Virginia Tech. Since the information under study is class assignments, the above is true whether you participate in the research or not. The results of this research study may be presented in summary form at conferences, in presentations, reports to the sponsor, academic papers, and as part of a thesis/dissertation.

column38: I used it both in a browser and in Eclipse, but I mostly used it in the browser so I checked that. Copilot is great mainly for code completion, because Eclipse's version is pretty awful in my opinion. My main use for ChatGPT was writing tests, which it actually excelled at. Instead of asking it to design tests, I looked through the mutation failures myself and visualized the state of the various objects. I then wrote down on index cards test layout to test specific states caused by mutations. It was much faster to just write out the test design without actually having to write code or come up with placeholder strings. When I was at a good place, I would send these designs to ChatGPT and have it create the code for me. This worked very well, as I left the thinking and design to me, while leaving the brute force and time-consuming work to the LLM.
